philosophical_distinction.is: Earning a return on value materially created by public capital, public land, public infrastructure, or exclusive public rights

public_risk_rule: If the public takes meaningful downside risk, it should not automatically receive only taxes while private owners keep all upside. If private capital carries nearly all risk, the state is not entitled to most of the return.
count_rule: COUNTABLE NOW stays $0 unless a candidate survives cash-flow math, capital costs, debt service, O&M, legal authority, and stress testing — and is truly incremental after pledges.

legal_anchors.label: Ark. Const. amend. 78 + A.C.A. § 14-168-301 et seq. (redevelopment / TIF)
legal_anchors.note: Increment typically pledged to project costs/bonds; URT diversion constrained (City of Fayetteville v. Washington County, 2007)

legal_anchors.label: Consolidated Incentive Act of 2003 / AEDC incentive stack
legal_anchors.note: Performance incentives + clawbacks today; participation upside redesign legal-pending

legal_anchors.label: A.C.A. § 14-362-101 et seq. regional airport authorities
legal_anchors.note: Revenue-bond / enterprise model; fees and rents pledged to airport system

legal_anchors.label: Amendment 65 / A.C.A. § 14-164-201 et seq. industrial development revenue bonds
legal_anchors.note: Often conduit — financing tool, not public operating surplus

candidates.name: Tax increment financing / Amendment 78 redevelopment districts
candidates.philosophical_class: EARN_RETURN_ON_PUBLICLY_ENABLED_APPRECIATION — but currently captures tax increment into project debt, not new public income
candidates.capital_required: Project-specific public infrastructure / land assembly (highly variable; often bond-financed)
candidates.financing_source: Tax increment bonds secured by incremental ad valorem revenues (Ark. Const. amend. 78; A.C.A. § 14-168-301 et seq.)
candidates.ownership_or_contract_structure: Local redevelopment district special fund; increments remitted to pay project costs and bonds
candidates.gross_revenue: Tax increment on rising AV inside district — statewide surplus series NEE
candidates.om: District/project admin; usually small vs debt
candidates.debt_service: Typically absorbs most/all increment while bonds outstanding
candidates.net_distributable_cash: Usually ~$0 to Tax Retirement Fund during debt life; may free local capacity only after bonds retire
candidates.downside_case: Project underperforms → shortfall; political pressure for other taxes; school-funding conflicts (URT diversion constrained — City of Fayetteville v. Washington County, 2007)
candidates.legal_authority: Amendment 78 + A.C.A. § 14-168-301 et seq.; URT/school mill constraints material
candidates.state_local_split: Primarily LOCAL district; not a state IIT replacement stream

public_risk_at_risk.what_public_risks: Bond repayment depends on increment; opportunity cost of diverted millages; blight/development risk
public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Mostly private land appreciation + project completion; public keeps dedicated increment for debt, not free surplus
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: If public takes development/credit risk, redesign should retain equity/participation — current TIF usually does not

candidates.notes: Useful local tool; fails as statewide IIT/property replacement engine because increments are pledged and school URT cannot be casually diverted

candidates.name: Infrastructure participation / upside-sharing development agreements
candidates.capital_required: Site infrastructure, roads, utilities, rail, pad-ready land — often tens of millions per mega-project
candidates.financing_source: State/local capital, AEDC packages, federal grants, private match
candidates.ownership_or_contract_structure: Contractual revenue share, ground lease, warrants/equity where lawful, or clawback+participation hybrid
candidates.gross_revenue: UNMODELED — no statewide inventory of participation cash flows
candidates.debt_service: If public borrowed for site work, debt must be covered first
candidates.downside_case: Firm underperforms / relocates; participation rights poorly drafted; political giveaway culture persists
candidates.legal_authority: LEGAL_PENDING for standardized statewide templates; gift/loan of credit and incentive statute interactions must be mapped

public_risk_at_risk.what_public_risks: Sunk infrastructure if jobs/payroll fail; incentive fiscal cost
public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Often private captures land/enterprise appreciation while public hopes for jobs/taxes
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: PASS philosophically if public capital material → public contractual upside; FAIL current practice when incentives are pure giveaways

candidates.notes: Core redesign of AEDC-style deals: participation instead of one-way subsidy

candidates.name: Ground leases on public land / publicly assembled sites
candidates.philosophical_class: FEE_RENT_ROYALTY on exclusive public land rights
candidates.capital_required: Land basis + any vertical improvements public funds
candidates.financing_source: Existing public land inventory or acquisition bonds
candidates.ownership_or_contract_structure: Long-term ground lease; rent + periodic reappraisal / percentage rent
candidates.gross_revenue: Lease rent — statewide public-land rent roll NEE
candidates.debt_service: If land was debt-financed, cover first
candidates.legal_authority: Local/state property lease powers; gift-of-public-property constraints

public_risk_at_risk.what_public_risks: Opportunity cost of land; lessee default
public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Public should keep residual land value + rent
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: Strong — exclusive public land rights justify rent; do not confuse with taxing privately created value alone

candidates.notes: Inventory-first; market-rate leases can feed local prosperity / Tax Retirement Fund only if not already agency-pledged

candidates.name: Revenue / profit participation agreements on publicly capitalized private enterprises
candidates.capital_required: Depends on public contribution (cash, land, infra, guarantees)
candidates.gross_revenue: UNMODELED — few standardized Arkansas statewide examples bound
candidates.debt_service: Private or public depending on structure
candidates.legal_authority: LEGAL_PENDING — must avoid unlawful private benefit / gift issues

public_risk_at_risk.what_public_risks: If guarantee/subsidy, public downside is real
public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Should scale with public risk — not a claim on all private return when private bears risk
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: PUBLIC_RISK_AT_RISK must set ceiling/floor of public claim

candidates.notes: Template + pilot deals required before any count

candidates.name: AEDC / Consolidated Incentive Act packages — redesign from giveaway to participation
candidates.capital_required: Foregone tax / rebate / credit cost is public fiscal capital
candidates.financing_source: State GR / tax expenditures (Create Rebate, Tax Back, InvestArk-class tools)
candidates.ownership_or_contract_structure: Today: performance agreement + clawback; Target: clawback + upside participation / equity-like rights
candidates.gross_revenue: Current model produces tax reduction, not public cash inflow
candidates.net_distributable_cash: Current countable incremental public income: $0 (cost center). Redesign UNMODELED
candidates.downside_case: Jobs fail → clawback incomplete; upside never shared
candidates.legal_authority: Consolidated Incentive Act of 2003 and successor rules; redesign needs statute/rule change

public_risk_at_risk.what_public_risks: Foregone revenue + political risk if firm leaves
public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Private enterprise upside; public gets hoped-for jobs/taxes
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: FAIL under current practice — public risk without commensurate upside claim

candidates.notes: Not countable until redesigned deals produce demonstrated net cash to reserved funds

candidates.name: Rights-of-way / utility corridor access charges
candidates.philosophical_class: FEE_RENT_ROYALTY on exclusive public corridor rights
candidates.ownership_or_contract_structure: Franchise fees, access charges, colocation rents
candidates.gross_revenue: Local franchise/ROW fees exist but statewide replacement-quality series NEE
candidates.reserves: Often general fund or utility fund — already spent
candidates.net_distributable_cash: UNMODELED incremental; existing fees typically already spent locally
candidates.legal_authority: Municipal franchise / ROW statutes; airport access fee powers example in A.C.A. § 14-362-109

public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Should be public rent for exclusive use of public ways
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: Good micro-engine; watch household incidence via utility bills

candidates.notes: Supportive local rent; not $7B-scale unless bundled into Enterprise broadband/energy ownership

candidates.name: Public land development / disposition with retained participation
candidates.capital_required: Entitlement, infrastructure, vertical if public develops
candidates.ownership_or_contract_structure: Sale with clawback/participation, ground lease, JV
candidates.gross_revenue: UNMODELED — state/local land bank inventory NEE
candidates.legal_authority: Public property disposition rules; gift constraints

public_risk_at_risk.what_public_risks: Construction/market risk if public develops; opportunity cost if sells cheap
public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Should retain residual claim if public land creates the location rent
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: Strong when public land is the scarce input

candidates.notes: Requires statewide public land / surplus property inventory before modeling

candidates.name: Airport authorities / municipal airport enterprises
candidates.capital_required: Runways, terminals, PFC-eligible projects — large, often federally constrained
candidates.financing_source: Airport revenue bonds, PFCs, FAA grants, airline rates
candidates.ownership_or_contract_structure: Airport authority / city enterprise; revenue bonds payable from airport revenues (A.C.A. § 14-362-101 et seq.)
candidates.gross_revenue: Airline rates, concessions, parking, fuel flowage — statewide net surplus NEE
candidates.debt_service: Typically absorbs free cash under indentures
candidates.net_distributable_cash: Usually $0 transferable to Tax Retirement Fund without violating bond/grant assurances
candidates.downside_case: Traffic shock; federal grant assurance limits on diversion

public_risk_at_risk.what_public_risks: Enterprise credit; residual taxpayer pressure if politics convert to GO support
public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Retained in airport system by design
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: Public owns asset, but cash is not free replacement income while pledged

candidates.notes: Real enterprise — wrong place to raid for IIT replacement

candidates.name: Ports, intermodal, and public industrial parks
candidates.capital_required: Docks, rail, warehouses, site prep — project finance scale
candidates.financing_source: Port authority revenue bonds, local capital, federal grants (e.g., Little Rock Port Authority structures)
candidates.ownership_or_contract_structure: Port/industrial park authority; leases to private operators; sometimes industrial park revenues ring-fenced separately from port terminal revenues
candidates.gross_revenue: Lease/tariff income — authority-level; no statewide net surplus bind this slice
candidates.debt_service: Often first claim on net revenues
candidates.legal_authority: Port authority statutes (e.g., A.C.A. Title 14, Ch. 186 class); industrial development bond frameworks

public_risk_at_risk.what_public_risks: Construction and occupancy risk on public balance sheet / authority credit
public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Should include ground-lease + participation when public builds the park
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: Strong enterprise candidate IF net cash after debt is reserved — unproven statewide

candidates.notes: Promising local enterprise class; needs audited net-cash survey before any count

candidates.name: Industrial development revenue bonds / conduit financing (Act 9-style)
candidates.philosophical_class: MOSTLY_CONDUIT — public title temporarily; private risk/return
candidates.capital_required: Project capital financed by bonds loaned/leased to private firm
candidates.ownership_or_contract_structure: Issuer holds title/leasehold for financing; company pays lease/loan; PILOTs common
candidates.gross_revenue: Bond debt service from company — not public operating profit
candidates.net_distributable_cash: Typically issuer fees only — not material replacement dollars
candidates.downside_case: If structure is not true conduit, public may absorb risk without upside
candidates.legal_authority: Amendment 65 / A.C.A. § 14-164-201 et seq. class industrial development bonds

public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Private keeps enterprise upside; public may abate taxes
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: If public risk ≈ 0, public claim on returns should be limited to fees/PILOT design — not pretend ownership return

candidates.notes: Financing tool ≠ productive public ownership return

candidates.name: Public energy infrastructure participation / ownership interests
candidates.financing_source: Utility rates, public bonds, private JV, federal programs
candidates.ownership_or_contract_structure: Public power / JV / lease / dividend rights
candidates.gross_revenue: UNMODELED — no statewide public energy dividend series bound
candidates.legal_authority: Utility regulation + public corporation law; overlaps Energy Sovereignty research

public_risk_at_risk.what_public_risks: Capital loss, operating loss, political rate risk
public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Should include dividends/lease rent if public owns/enables
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: Matches philosophy — but capital path and years-to-scale required before count

candidates.notes: Likely major long-run engine with Prosperity Fund; zero now

candidates.name: Public / public-participation broadband networks
candidates.financing_source: Federal/state grants, revenue bonds, co-op equity
candidates.gross_revenue: Subscriber/wholesale — statewide public net surplus NEE
candidates.net_distributable_cash: Often $0 after O&M/debt in early years; grants may restrict diversions

public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Should include wholesale dividends if public owns
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: Valid enterprise — not countable without audited free cash

candidates.notes: Strategic External Income enabler; replacement cash unproven

candidates.name: Water / wastewater enterprise utilities
candidates.net_distributable_cash: $0 for Tax Retirement Fund without raising household rates (fails prosperity design)
candidates.downside_case: Affordability crisis if raided for general revenue

public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Should fund system resilience, not IIT replacement
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: NOT suitable as household-burden replacement engine

candidates.notes: Keep as Use/cost-recovery; do not convert into IIT swap

candidates.name: Research / IP commercialization from publicly financed R&D
candidates.ownership_or_contract_structure: Licenses, equity in spinouts, royalty shares
candidates.gross_revenue: UNMODELED statewide public IP royalty ledger
candidates.downside_case: Most IP earns little; blockbuster rare
candidates.legal_authority: University IP policies; Bayh-Dole interactions for federal funds

public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Public should retain royalty/equity where public financed the science
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: Correct direction; not a near-term scale engine

candidates.notes: External Income / Prosperity Fund feeder over decades

candidates.name: Public housing infrastructure / land + vertical participation
candidates.net_distributable_cash: Typically $0 by design (affordability), not Tax Retirement Fund
candidates.downside_case: Raiding affordable housing cash for tax replacement would be unsuitable

public_risk_at_risk.upside_today: Social return primary; financial surplus secondary
public_risk_at_risk.alignment_test: NOT suitable as primary IIT replacement engine

candidates.notes: May support community prosperity goals without counting as tax-replacement cash

COUNTABLE_NOW.verdict: EMPTY — no candidate cleared full cash-flow + legal + stress gates as free incremental replacement dollars

PLAUSIBLE_BUT_UNMODELED_LEGAL_PENDING.verdict: Infrastructure participation redesign; ground leases; revenue shares; AEDC participation conversion; public land development; ports/industrial parks net cash survey; energy/broadband ownership; research IP royalties

NOT_MATERIAL_AS_REPLACEMENT_ENGINE.verdict: TIF increments (pledged); ROW fees (local/small); airports (pledged); conduit IDBs (not ownership returns); water enterprises and housing (must not be raided)

engine_role_verdict.VALUE_CAPTURE: STRATEGICALLY_CENTRAL_BUT_UNMODELED — current Arkansas practice often gives public risk without upside; redesign path is real, countable cash is not
engine_role_verdict.ENTERPRISE: REAL_ASSETS_EXIST_BUT_CASH_IS_PLEDGED_OR_UNSURVEYED — airports/ports/utilities are enterprises, not free Tax Retirement Fund deposits
engine_role_verdict.scale_implication: With Use/Depletion/Value Capture/Enterprise still at $0 countable, large-scale replacement burden shifts decisively toward Human-capital, Prosperity Fund, and External Income modeling
